values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/goosecreekforest ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground'; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Goose Creek State Forest Campground), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Many places in the campground to reach the river (paddling, trout fishing).

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/goosecreekforest ('There are vault toilets.' 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well.' 'There are many places throughout the campground to access the river.'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 'Nine sites for tent and small trailer use, all of which have a view of the river' (DNR page; the amenity table says 12). No length limit posted. One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/goosecreekforest ('There are nine sites for tent and small trailer use, all of which have a view of the river', 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Goose Creek State Forest Campground: 12 campsites), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Open all year, but the campground and seasonal roads are not plowed.

season.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/goosecreekforest ('This rustic campground is open all year; however, the campground and seasonal roads are not plowed.') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Goose Creek State Forest Campground: Seasonal closure dates 'open all year'), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic state forest campground under red pine and hardwoods on the shore of the Upper Manistee River, 5.5 mi W of Frederic via County Road 612 and Manistee River Road (Crawford County); managed by Hartwick Pines State Park. Many river access points for paddling and trout fishing. Reached by driving through the attached Goose Creek Trail Camp (a group equestrian camp) from their shared entrance. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: $20 at the kiosk + Recreation Passport, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come only, 15-day maximum (inherited max now confirmed), open all year (roads not plowed). Changed site count 12 -> 9 (DNR page: 'nine sites'; the table still says 12). Phone 989-348-7068 matches (Hartwick Pines SP). Note trimmed of field restatements.
flags: Website is the generic state-forest-campgrounds page; the campground's own DNR page is https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/goosecreekforest.
Waterfront re-audit lead: the DNR page says the campground 'sits on the shore of the Upper Manistee River' and its nine sites 'all ... have a view of the river'; the entry has 'not waterfront'.

Horse-camp check: the amenity table types Goose Creek State Forest Campground 'rustic' and only the attached Goose Creek Trail Camp 'equestrian - group'. The DNR page: 'The Goose Creek Trail Camp is attached to this campground and to get to the Goose Creek State Forest Campground you must drive through the Trail Camp. Both campgrounds are accessed through the same entrance off Manistee River Road.' So the campground itself is not a horse camp, but the two are separate camps sharing one entrance road, and you drive through the horse camp to reach it.
